text: Hi there! I'm PIP, and this is Mailwing, our mail ship.
We work for Cosmic Mail. We carry the stories of space explorers all the way home to Earth.
Every explorer has a file in the Cosmic Archive.
Look how they're all connected!
Oh! That file just lost its connection.
And another one, and another... They're all going dark!
Wait... Mailwing just detected something unusual!
Oh! A powerful solar storm!
It sent energy and particles into space, disrupting our communication network!
The storm disrupted the Archive while its memories were being updated!
Now some of the explorers' stories are incomplete!
The Archive is trying to fix them...
But the pieces don't fit together!
And some of my own memories are missing too.
I know these explorers... but I can't remember what they discovered.
Wait! I still remember two places where their signals came from!
If we fly there, we can find the explorers and recover their missing stories!
Lots of explorers' stories are still waiting to be remembered.
We can find them, rebuild their memories, and send their stories home!
So... will you help me?
Let's make your Carrier ID! Type your name on the screen.
Your Carrier ID is saved in your mission album. Come on, I'll show you the cabin.
Your mission album is on the console. Let me open it for you!
This is your Cosmic Album! Here you see your carrier badge and how far we've come.
Each card is an explorer we're looking for. It fills up as we find it and send its story home.
Now the Discoveries page, our photo lab! Every part you scan opens a new photo and a new fact.
And here are your Stamps! Every story we deliver to Earth earns one.
You can open your album any time, even while exploring. I'll close it for now.
Next, the navigation screen! It shows where the signals are coming from.
These are the places we can fly to. Tap one with a signal.
Great choice! Now tap Confirm route to set our course.
Welcome back, carrier! The Archive is waiting for our next delivery.
Route ready! Now press the big red button to take off.
Here we go. Let's bring this memory home.
We're here, explorer! The signal is somewhere ahead, let's go take a peek!
We made it to Mars! You flew like a real space carrier.
Listen! My antenna hears a tiny signal, and something out there needs our help.
To find it, we have a radar. It shows us where to go next.
Before we go, you need to know two tools. Let's start with the Radar!
The orange star shows where to go. Turn until it is at the top, then walk straight ahead!
Great job! Now let's look at the Scanner.
The scanner looks at things up close. Aim at something that glows and hold to scan.
You're ready, carrier! Let's follow the signal together.
Follow the orange star on your radar. It leads to our practice rock!
Look, a glowing practice rock! Let's try your scanner on it.
Scan complete, you did it! Now let's follow the star to the signal.
Let's walk to the practice rock first. Follow the star!
Let's practice with the scanner first, then we'll take a closer look.
Whoa, look over there! Could that be our missing explorer?
Shh, it's an old rover napping in the dust! Press E to take a closer look.
Shh, it's an old rover napping in the dust! Tap Inspect to take a closer look.
Clue one: find the rover's eyes! They're way up at the top of its tall mast.
Clue two: find the rock tool! It's on the arm, down low at the front.
Last clue: find the heat reader! It peeked out through the mast, just below the eyes.
Beep boop, I remember now! This is Opportunity, a rover that hunted for clues about ancient water.
Let's help it remember! Press Q to grab your scanner.
Let's help it remember! Tap the scanner button to grab it.
Yes, the eyes! Opportunity's cameras took giant pictures, so scientists could pick where to drive.
Grind, grind! This tool scraped off a rock's dusty skin, so scientists could study the fresh rock inside.
This one could see invisible heat light! It found minerals that showed water was once here.
Psst! Look up high, at the top of the mast!
Psst! Check the arm, down low at the front!
Psst! Look at the tall mast, just below the eyes!
The eyes are still missing! Aim at the top of the mast and hold the scan button.
The rock tool is still missing! Aim at the arm, down low, and hold the scan button.
The heat reader is still missing! Aim at the mast, below the eyes, and hold the scan button.
Woohoo, all three parts! Its memory is coming back!
Sealed! Tap Watch its story to see Opportunity's adventure.
Story delivered! Follow the star back to our ship, explorer.
We're helping this explorer remember its parts. Follow the star on your radar!
Its tools are on the tall mast and on the arm. Aim there and hold to scan!
Try your scanner on the mast and the arm, explorer!
Some parts are still missing. The explorer is waiting for us!
The letter is ready! Let's walk back to our ship.
This story is safe on Earth now. Great job, explorer!
Its memory is back! Seal the letter, then let's walk back to our ship.
This story is safe now! You can see it in your mission album anytime.
The air here is super thin. Every dust grain has been waiting a looong time!
Those rocks look ancient. I bet they have amazing stories!
We did it! Opportunity is quiet now, but its discoveries will never be forgotten.
The Cosmic Scanner can read the landscape too. Aim at a big rock or a layered outcrop and hold the scan.
Beep boop, I remember now! This is Spirit, a rover that read the rocks for clues about ancient water.
Yes, the eyes! Spirit's cameras took giant pictures, so scientists could pick where to drive.
Its memory is back! Tap Seal the letter to keep its story safe.
Sealed! Tap Watch its story to see Spirit's adventure.
Record saved! Now tap the big button and send it home to Earth!
Whoosh, it made it! The story is safe on Earth, and you earned a new stamp!
We did it! Spirit is quiet now, but its discoveries will never be forgotten.
Not yet, explorer! Let's find all three parts first, I'll help you!
Almost there! Hold the scan on the practice rock, you can do it!
We're here! Press Q to take out your scanner.
We're here! Tap the scanner button to take it out.
There's our ship! Press E to climb aboard.
There's our ship! Tap Board to climb aboard.
Look, it's Mars! Three old explorers are hiding down there, tap a glowing spot to pick one!
That's Meridiani Planum, a wide flat plain. Someone is waiting there!
That's Gusev Crater, a giant bowl in the ground. Someone is waiting there!
Hold on tight, we're going down!
We have a story aboard! Let's watch it and send it to Earth.
Another story saved! Let's visit the next explorer, tap a glowing spot!
We already saved this story! Let's try another spot.
Every story here is safe! Let's fly home to the cabin, explorer.
We made it to the Moon! You flew like a real space carrier.
We're on the Moon, explorer! No air and no wind, just gray dust and a signal to follow!
Whoa, look over there! Something shiny is sitting in the dust.
Shh, an old machine is resting here! Press E to take a closer look.
Shh, an old machine is resting here! Tap Inspect to take a closer look.
There's no wind on the Moon, so footprints here can last for a very, very long time!
Look up! That blue ball in the black sky is Earth, our home.
Look, it's the Moon! Two old explorers are waiting down there, tap a glowing spot to pick one!
That's the Sea of Tranquility, a wide flat plain. Someone is waiting there!
That's the Ocean of Storms, with a small crater in it. Someone is waiting there!
Beep boop, I remember now! This is Surveyor 3, a robot that tested the Moon's ground before astronauts came.
Clue one: find the lander's eye! It's a tall camera with a little mirror hood.
Clue two: find the digging scoop! It's at the end of a folding arm, down low.
Last clue: find the radar! It's tucked under the body, looking down at the ground.
Click, click! This camera sent thousands of pictures of the Moon home to Earth.
Dig, dig! This scoop made little trenches to test if the ground was strong enough to stand on.
Beep, beep! This radar measured how high and how fast Surveyor 3 was while it came down.
Psst! Look for the tall camera on the side!
Psst! Look low, at the end of the folding arm!
Psst! Look under the body, near the ground!
The eye is still missing! Aim at the tall camera and hold the scan button.
The scoop is still missing! Aim low, at the end of the arm, and hold the scan button.
The radar is still missing! Aim under the body and hold the scan button.
Its tools are the tall camera, the folding arm and the radar underneath. Aim there and hold to scan!
Try your scanner on the camera, the arm and under the body, explorer!
Sealed! Tap Watch its story to see Surveyor 3's adventure.
We did it! Surveyor 3 is quiet now, but it helped astronauts land safely on the Moon.
Beep boop, I remember now! This is Eagle, the lander that carried the first people to walk on the Moon.
Clue one: find the feeler! A long thin rod is lying flat in the dust beside a footpad.
Clue two: find the engine! It's the big bell hiding under the gold body.
Last clue: find the plaque! It's a small metal sign on the leg with the ladder.
Contact! When this feeler touched the Moon, a light turned on inside Eagle.
Whoosh! This engine could push softly or strongly, so Eagle could land gently.
This sign says they came in peace for all mankind. That means everyone, everywhere!
Psst! Look down in the dust, next to a big round foot!
Psst! Look under the middle of the gold body!
Psst! Look at the leg with the ladder!
The feeler is still missing! Aim at the thin rod on the ground and hold the scan button.
The engine is still missing! Aim under the gold body and hold the scan button.
The plaque is still missing! Aim at the ladder leg and hold the scan button.
Its parts are the feeler on the ground, the engine underneath and the plaque by the ladder. Aim and hold to scan!
Try your scanner on the ground by the feet, under the body and on the ladder leg, explorer!
Sealed! Tap Watch its story to see Eagle's adventure.
We did it! Eagle still stands on the Moon, keeping its message of peace.
A solar panel that turned sunlight into power! Nice find, but it won't unlock a memory fragment.
Three legs with squishy footpads for a soft landing. Important, but not a fragment.
This flat antenna sent the pictures home. Good to know, but not a fragment.
Four strong legs with big round feet! Important, but they won't unlock a memory fragment.
The famous ladder, where the first steps on the Moon began! Nice find, but not a fragment.
Solar panels, and the wind even cleaned them once! Nice find, but they won't unlock a memory fragment.
Six wheels carried Opportunity farther than a marathon. They're important, but this is not a memory fragment.
Antennas helped Opportunity send its pictures home. Good to know, but not a fragment.
Solar panels that gave Spirit its power! Nice find, but they won't unlock a memory fragment.
Six wheels carried Spirit across Mars. They're important, but this is not a memory fragment.
Antennas helped Spirit send its data home through orbiters. Good to know, but not a fragment.
Let us stay on the signal trail.
Later, pilot. The signal first.
Inspect it first (E).
Drag the joystick to walk and drag the screen to look around.
Walk with WASD and move the mouse to look around.
Tap the scanner button, aim at the glowing rock and hold Scan.
Press Q, aim at the glowing rock and hold the left mouse button.
Turn until the orange star is at the top of the radar, then walk.
The signal is near. Walk up to the shape and press E.
I'm picking up another faint signal. It's still too weak to follow, but the Archive has marked it for later.
This dark rock looks volcanic. I am comparing its shape and tone with Martian basalt references.
This looks like fine Martian dust over broken rock. The surface is loose and easy for the wind to move.
These streaks look shaped by the wind. The scanner is reading the ripple pattern, not the weather.
This layered outcrop may record ancient changes. The scanner sees stacked layers worth a closer look.
Beep boop, I remember now! This is Viking 1, one of the first explorers to search for life on Mars.
Clue one: find the lander's eyes! Two round cameras stand on top of its body.
Clue two: find the digging arm! It reaches out from the front, down low.
Last clue: find the dish! It sits on a mast, pointed at the sky.
Click! These cameras took the very first picture ever made on the ground of Mars.
Scoop! This arm dug up Martian soil so the tiny labs inside could look for signs of life.
Beep beep! This dish sent Viking's pictures and weather reports straight home to Earth.
Psst! Look on top of the body for two round towers!
Psst! Look at the front, down low, for a long arm!
Psst! Look up high for a round dish!
The eyes are still missing! Aim at the two round cameras and hold the scan button.
The arm is still missing! Aim at the long arm in front and hold the scan button.
The dish is still missing! Aim at the round dish up high and hold the scan button.
Its tools are the cameras on top, the arm in front and the dish up high. Aim there and hold to scan!
Try your scanner on the cameras, the arm and the dish, explorer!
Sealed! Tap Watch its story to see Viking's adventure.
We did it! Viking 1 is quiet now, but its search for life still inspires explorers today.
That's Chryse Planitia, a wide golden plain. Someone is waiting there!
Sturdy legs with round feet! Important, but they won't unlock a memory fragment.
1 of 5 stories restored. Great work, carrier!
2 of 5 stories restored. Great work, carrier!
3 of 5 stories restored. Great work, carrier!
4 of 5 stories restored. Great work, carrier!
